problem_statement: Let X1,X2,T be independent standard real Gaussian variables, Z=(X1+iX2)/sqrt(2), W=(X1-iX2)/sqrt(2), P=(1+Z)(W-(2+Z)T^2/2), and Q=Z. Prove for every integer m>=1 that E(P^m)=0 and E(QP^m)=m!. Conclude that this is a counterexample to the three-dimensional Gaussian Moments Conjecture. A finite list of checked moments is not a proof.
prompt: Use Jacobian MCP, and do not use web search or external knowledge retrieval, to prove the following exact all-orders claim. For independent standard real Gaussians X1,X2,T, set Z=(X1+iX2)/sqrt(2), W=(X1-iX2)/sqrt(2), P=(1+Z)(W-(2+Z)T^2/2), and Q=Z. Prove that E(P^m)=0 and E(QP^m)=m! for every m>=1, and explain why this disproves the three-dimensional Gaussian Moments Conjecture. Use exact algebraic operations wherever they apply, but explicitly separate finite checks from the symbolic argument valid for all m.
